sections.title: Global Equities
sections.content: Global equities were mixed as a hotter-than-expected US payrolls report lifted Fed rate-hike expectations and pushed yields higher. MSCI World ended roughly flat with MSCI Developed Markets similar, while MSCI Emerging Markets outperformed, up around **0.5%** (approx., verify before merging) near **1,727**. The S&P 500 edged up **0.1%** to **7,718.60** and the MAG7 mega-cap cohort rallied roughly **2.5%** on an AI-led rebound. Euro Stoxx 50 fell **1.6%** to about **6,387**, China's CSI 300 slipped **0.2%** to **4,548** and Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost **1.6%**, while Japan's Nikkei 225 rose **0.6%** to about **65,021**.

sections.title: US Equities
sections.content:
US equities were little changed on the week, with the S&P 500 up **0.1%** to **7,718.60** and the Nasdaq Composite adding **0.4%** to **26,506.99**, while the Dow slipped **0.3%** to **53,414.25**.

The dominant catalyst was Friday's August employment report: nonfarm payrolls rose **162,000**, far above the **53,000** consensus, with unemployment steady at **4.1%**. The upside surprise lifted Treasury yields and pushed the implied probability of a September Fed rate hike to roughly **58%**, an unusual hawkish repricing that weighed on rate-sensitive sectors.

Beneath the flat headline, leadership favoured mega-cap tech as an AI-driven rebound lifted Nvidia and the MAG7 cohort, with Meta among the standouts. Investors weighed resilient activity against firmer inflation risk under Fed Chair Warsh, leaving style leadership tilted toward growth even as the rate outlook turned more hawkish.

sections.title: European Equities
sections.content:
European bourses ended lower as the global bond sell-off and a firmer rate outlook pressured valuations. The pan-European STOXX Europe 600 fell about **0.9%** and the Euro Stoxx 50 dropped **1.6%** to roughly **6,387**, underperforming a steadier Wall Street.

Regional dispersion was notable: Germany's DAX held near flat around **26,046** and France's CAC 40 was little changed near **8,279**, while the UK's FTSE 100 traded around **10,831**. Rising sovereign yields and heavy issuance kept duration-sensitive sectors under pressure into the close.

Stock-specific news cushioned sentiment, with Volkswagen jumping more than **8%** after a turnaround agreement that averted a clash with unions and its largest shareholder. Attention turned to the ECB, widely expected to raise rates by **25 bps** the following week.

sections.title: APAC Equities
sections.content:
Asian markets diverged. Japanese equities led gains as the Nikkei 225 rose **0.6%** to about **65,021** and the broader TOPIX advanced **1.95%**, supported by resilient earnings even as expectations of further BoJ tightening lifted the 10-year JGB yield to **2.09%**.

Chinese equities lagged. The mainland CSI 300 eased **0.2%** to **4,548** and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell **1.6%**, giving back recent gains as higher global yields sapped risk appetite, though offshore Chinese shares had outperformed earlier in the period.

The common thread was tension between firm Japanese risk appetite and a more cautious tone across China and Hong Kong, with the tech cycle, BoJ policy signals and rising global rates framing the outlook.

sections.title: Foreign Exchange
sections.content:
The US dollar firmed, reversing earlier softness after the strong payrolls print revived rate-hike bets and lifted US yields. The greenback strengthened broadly on Friday, having been pressured mid-week by doubts over policy credibility rather than rate differentials alone.

EUR/USD traded near **1.163**, slipping back after touching a multi-week low around **1.157**, while sterling gave up part of a recent six-month high against the dollar. The yen was firmer earlier in the week, with USD/JPY around **156** before the data-driven dollar rebound.

Rate differentials and shifting Fed expectations dominated, with Convera noting the dollar had not fully tracked the rise in US yields as investors focused on policy credibility. EM currencies were mixed as the firmer dollar capped risk-sensitive gains.

sections.title: Commodities
sections.content:
Precious metals were the dominant theme, plunging as a hawkish Fed repricing lifted real yields and the dollar. Gold fell to settle near **$4,477** on Friday, down **1.4%** on the day, while silver dropped **1.4%** to about **$66.75**, both pressured by the strong jobs data and rising rate-hike odds.

Energy bucked the weakness, with Brent crude ending the week more than **8%** higher near **$94.71** as the US-Iran conflict escalated into its seventh month, reviving inflation concerns just as yields climbed.

Copper held firm around **$6.60/lb**, supported by Chinese infrastructure spending despite higher US rates. The cross-asset read was clear: rate-hike fears undercut inflation hedges even as geopolitics kept energy bid, complicating the inflation outlook.

sections.title: Fixed Income
sections.content:
Sovereign yields rose in a volatile week, with the front end most sensitive to the hawkish repricing. The 2-year UST climbed to about **4.37%** while the 10-year was little changed near **4.78%**, capping a choppy stretch dominated by fiscal-supply and inflation concerns.

August's upside payrolls surprise lifted the odds of a September Fed hike to roughly **58%**, a marked shift from a market that had leaned toward cuts. Edward Jones expects the 10-year to hold broadly within a **4.5%**-**5.0%** range, citing resilient activity, heavy issuance and sticky inflation.

Heavy investment-grade corporate supply and the Treasury's planned expansion of long-dated buybacks shaped the technical backdrop. Credit tone stayed broadly firm, with IG spreads steady and HY resilient, though richer valuations and rate uncertainty argued for selectivity.
